lines.text: What if all the ice on Earth melted?
Not some of it. All of it.
Our planet holds over thirty million cubic kilometres of ice. About ninety percent of it sits on Antarctica.
But here's the twist. When floating sea ice melts, sea level barely moves. It's like ice in your drink.
The real danger is ice sitting on land.
Melt Greenland, and the oceans rise seven metres.
Melt Antarctica, and they rise almost sixty more.
That's around seventy metres. Taller than a twenty-story building.
Hundreds of millions of people would need a new home.
The good news? It would take thousands of years.
The bad news? The seas are already rising.
